name: FlowMail Campaigns
author: flowpressuk

sections.description:
FlowMail Campaigns helps site owners create, send, and measure email campaigns directly from WordPress. It includes subscriber management, forms, queued sending, templates, email logs, content update emails, scheduled campaigns, list-based automations, and optional WooCommerce automations when WooCommerce is installed and active.

All features described here are included and functional in this plugin.

Core features

  • Email campaigns with templates and placeholders.
  • Subscriber forms and subscriber management.
  • Internal Bot Shield for public forms with no third-party CAPTCHA service.
  • Native block editor blocks for FlowMail forms and subscriber update content.
  • Contact forms and selling enquiry forms.
  • Email queue, sent email history, and email results.
  • Subscriber preferences and unsubscribe handling.
  • Content publishing logs and content update emails.
  • Scheduled one-time and recurring campaigns.
  • Starter campaign sets for weekly emails and UK seasonal dates.
  • Optional WooCommerce automations when WooCommerce is installed and active.
  • WooCommerce product alerts for back-in-stock, price-drop, and product category new-arrival subscriptions.
  • Product alert automations management inside Automations, including category subscription overview and editable alert email templates.
  • Manual Google-style review badge and no-API copy/paste review imports.
  • Health check and setup tools.

External services

FlowMail Campaigns does not send operational data to FlowPress or to a fixed external API.

By default, emails are sent through WordPress using wp_mail(), which uses the site’s own mail configuration. If the site administrator enables the optional custom SMTP setting, outgoing email is sent to the SMTP server entered by that administrator when an email is sent. Depending on the email being sent, this can include recipient email addresses, sender details, subject lines, message content, and technical email headers.

The SMTP server is not supplied by FlowMail Campaigns and is not required for the plugin to work. Site administrators who enter their own SMTP server details should review the terms and privacy policy for that chosen mail provider.

The plugin also includes an admin-only WP-Cron loopback diagnostic. When an administrator runs that diagnostic, the site sends a request to its own wp-cron.php URL to confirm that scheduled tasks can run. No FlowPress service is contacted for this check.

The Reviews screen includes a manual Google-style review badge and a copy/paste importer for reviews that an administrator chooses to copy from their public Google review page. This feature does not contact Google, does not scrape Google, and does not use a Google API key.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the flowmail-campaigns folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or upload the ZIP through Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate FlowMail Campaigns from Plugins → Installed Plugins.
  3. Open FlowMail Campaigns → Settings to configure sender details, SMTP options, forms, and safety settings.
  4. Create your first campaign under FlowMail Campaigns → Campaigns.
sections.faq:
Does this use a third-party email service?

No external email platform is required by default. Emails are sent through your WordPress mail configuration. If you configure SMTP, email delivery is handled by the SMTP provider you choose.

What data is sent to external services?

FlowMail Campaigns does not send operational data to FlowPress. If SMTP is enabled, email data is sent to the configured SMTP provider when an email is sent. This can include recipient email addresses, sender details, subject lines, message content, and email headers.

Does FlowMail Campaigns connect to FlowPress?

No external FlowPress connection is required for plugin functionality. Links to FlowPress are provided for documentation, support, and product information only.

  • Added an inline explanation that routine queue, cron, watchdog, maintenance and recovery history remains available without inflating the main Activity totals.

  • Keeps abandoned-cart sweep history under System -> All technical and aggregates same-day passes, including the total carts marked abandoned.
  • Removed auto-discarded Bot Shield/spam form submissions from meaningful Activity while keeping held/blocked submissions visible when they need review.
  • Meaningful Activity KPI/filter totals now exclude those maintenance/spam housekeeping rows as well.

1.3.75

  • Keeps routine operational events under System -> All technical while warnings/failures remain visible in normal activity.
  • Tightens queue/system event classification so failures are never hidden by broad queue-runtime matching.
  • Activity KPI/filter counts now exclude hidden routine events; repetitive technical rows remain grouped.
  • Uses friendly full timestamps in the Activity timeline while keeping Upcoming separate and true Campaign/Automation types.

1.3.74

  • Added System detail controls on the Activity page: Important by default, with All technical available on demand. Routine technical events are grouped to keep the timeline readable.
  • Corrected Upcoming classification so scheduled/recurring date campaigns appear as Campaigns while genuine trigger-based sends remain Automations.
  • Updated Upcoming cards and dashboard activity timestamps to friendlier site-local date/time labels.
  • Kept system failures, overdue/held delivery problems and other actionable errors visible in the normal timeline while deeper diagnostic evidence remains in Health Check and Event Ledger.

1.3.73

  • Added a cross-app Activity timeline covering audience, purchases, campaigns, automations, reviews, content and system events.
  • Added a dedicated Activity workspace page with area, status, date and search filters.
  • Split future scheduled campaigns and queued emails into Upcoming so they are never presented as historical activity.
  • Updated the Overview Latest Activity panel to use the global timeline and added a compact Upcoming section.
  • Added Activity to the FlowMail workspace navigation and kept low-level technical events in Health Check / Event Ledger.

1.3.72

  • Fixed Notification Center queue alerts so future-scheduled pending emails remain normal Waiting to Send activity and do not count as items needing attention.
  • Added a 15-minute grace window after the scheduled send time before a pending email is treated as overdue, avoiding false alerts from ordinary WP-Cron timing.
  • Failed emails still alert immediately; held/paused emails only alert after their send time is overdue, and genuinely stuck processing items are surfaced.

1.3.71

  • Fixed core subscriber automation provenance so hourly Welcome follow-up, inactive, anniversary, birthday and lead-magnet scans record genuine live queue activity as Automatic instead of legacy/unknown.

  • Added a bounded one-time repair for legacy Subscriber anniversary queue/log rows whose activity date matches the subscriber join month/day, allowing Email Results and diagnostics to recognise historic automatic anniversary scan activity without treating unrelated legacy sends as proof.

1.3.70

  • Reworked the Subscribers Column guide into compact groups that mirror the table: Subscriber, Profile, Engagement, Customer, Acquisition & Preferences, and System.
  • Removed non-column material from the guide and moved inactivity-rule and bulk-action guidance into Help & Shortcuts.
  • Added concise hover tooltips to subscriber table column headings.
  • Made the guide remember its open/closed state and follow Essential/Full view, with the advanced Origin note shown only in Full view.

1.3.69

  • Cleaned the Subscribers Interest filter so it only shows customer-facing product/category topics instead of raw internal tags.
  • Merged duplicate interest/category aliases into one readable option and excluded product IDs, alert tags, birthdays, source tags, spam/admin metadata, and other system context.
  • Updated the Interest table column to show the same clean topic labels used by the filter.
  • Kept subscriber-selected email choices under Preference with clearer labels and renamed the table section to Acquisition & Preferences.
  • Kept the legacy Interest filter query key for bookmarked admin URLs while matching both historic interest: and category: storage aliases.

1.3.68

1.3.67

  • Adds completed-order count to the shared WooCommerce customer facts and calculates lifetime spend from completed orders only.
  • Clears cached purchase facts immediately when an order completes so New/Repeat/value-tier classification updates on the same request.
  • Adds a one-time background classification repair that removes stale managed customer tags while preserving acquisition, preference, origin, health and manual tags.
  • Hardens High-value/VIP safety scans so stale tags cannot dispatch value-tier automations to non-purchasers.

1.3.66

  • Adds Welcome email and Welcome follow-up milestones to the Subscriber Customer journey, including future scheduled welcome mail that automatically becomes a sent milestone after delivery.
  • Adds the latest genuine Subscriber anniversary milestone only after at least one full calendar year has passed since joining FlowMail.
  • Enriches a valid anniversary milestone with the anniversary email subject when that email was sent.
  • Keeps the historic same-year anniversary misfire visible in Email engagement as factual send history, but excludes it from Customer journey so it is never presented as a real anniversary.

1.3.65

  • Prevents Subscriber anniversary from firing in the subscriber’s original signup year; the first anniversary is now one full calendar year after joining.
  • Keeps anniversary sends recurring annually on the join month/day after the first year, with the existing per-anniversary de-duplication.
  • Updates Customer Simulation and testing guidance so same-year join dates correctly report that the first anniversary has not yet been reached.
  • Clarifies anniversary wording in automation descriptions and diagnostics.

1.3.64

  • Automation firing diagnostics now separate scheduled, due-soon and genuinely attention-needed queue items.
  • Waiting to Send sidebar counts remain informational blue when all queued mail is scheduled normally, turning amber only when something is overdue, held, paused, failed or stuck processing.
  • Uses canonical automation display names in automation firing diagnostics.

1.3.63

  • Compacts engagement emails individually when their detailed open/click/site/order evidence has expired, even if newer retained engagement events still exist for the same subscriber.
  • Replaces repeated empty engagement-stage boxes with one scan-friendly row showing send time, canonical email name, source type, and an honest retained-detail status.
  • Keeps the full Sent → Opened → Clicked → Site activity → Order/goal journey only for emails that still have retained evidence.

  • Consolidates the subscriber profile into clearer Profile, Journey, Purchases, Subscriptions, Engagement, and Delivery areas.
  • Removes the duplicate Subscriber overview card and moves its unique identity and engagement details into the main profile context panel.

  • Combines double opt-in and bounce/suppression information in one Consent & delivery health section.
  • Makes Engagement journey the primary email-history view and moves raw sent/open/click tables into a collapsed Technical email records disclosure.
  • Compacts historical engagement journeys when detailed event rows have expired, avoiding repeated empty Opened/Clicked/Site/Order boxes.
  • Uses Imported to FlowMail wording in the at-a-glance summary when the subscriber was imported.

1.3.61

  • Adds All, Campaigns, Automations, and System filters plus Show all/Show fewer controls.
  • Distinguishes test emails and directly attributed WooCommerce orders.
  • Improves the Customer journey latest-engagement milestone with the actual email name/subject when retained tracking detail exists.

  • Added persistent collapsible profile sections with smart defaults, per-subscriber saved state, and Expand all / Collapse all controls in the sticky jump navigation.

1.3.50

  • Added standard suppression reason codes to queue records and audit evidence, including invalid recipient, inactive/missing subscriber, duplicate/abandoned-cart suppression and rate-limit outcomes.
  • Added a non-destructive production self-test covering database writes, cron scheduling, queue backlog, recorded delivery evidence, tracking and missed-trigger watchdog state, with compact System Health summaries on key admin pages.
  • Added campaign/automation configuration revision snapshots and restore controls so edits and status changes have rollback points.
  • Integrated Selected row actions with the existing Automation Testing Center: Test & diagnostics now opens the central testing tools already focused on the selected automation; Event ledger and Revision history are available alongside it. Manual/scheduled campaigns use delivery diagnostics and revisions without duplicating automation-only testing tools.
  • Added database indexes and configurable low-value ledger retention to keep the growing diagnostics/history data efficient while preserving important delivery, failure and suppression evidence.

  • System alert submissions now run the shared subscriber spam evaluator after Bot Shield, including rate/domain/email-pattern/name checks; blocked/held attempts do not create alert requests or confirmation emails.
  • Current subscribers / requests now shows a consistent Name, Email, Request/category, Date and Status view, while retaining detailed product-alert management controls.

  • Labels test rows clearly and explains that a delivery test proves render/queue/mail delivery, not a natural automation trigger.

short_description: Create email campaigns, manage subscribers, add forms, schedule sending, and view reports from WordPress.
description:
FlowMail Campaigns helps site owners create, send, and measure email campaigns directly from WordPress. It includes subscriber management, forms, queued sending, templates, email logs, content update emails, scheduled campaigns, list-based automations, and optional WooCommerce automations when WooCommerce is installed and active.

All features described here are included and functional in this plugin.

Core features

  • Email campaigns with templates and placeholders.
  • Subscriber forms and subscriber management.
  • Internal Bot Shield for public forms with no third-party CAPTCHA service.
  • Native block editor blocks for FlowMail forms and subscriber update content.
  • Contact forms and selling enquiry forms.
  • Email queue, sent email history, and email results.
  • Subscriber preferences and unsubscribe handling.
  • Content publishing logs and content update emails.
  • Scheduled one-time and recurring campaigns.
  • Starter campaign sets for weekly emails and UK seasonal dates.
  • Optional WooCommerce automations when WooCommerce is installed and active.
  • WooCommerce product alerts for back-in-stock, price-drop, and product category new-arrival subscriptions.
  • Product alert automations management inside Automations, including category subscription overview and editable alert email templates.
  • Manual Google-style review badge and no-API copy/paste review imports.
  • Health check and setup tools.

External services

FlowMail Campaigns does not send operational data to FlowPress or to a fixed external API.

By default, emails are sent through WordPress using wp_mail(), which uses the site’s own mail configuration. If the site administrator enables the optional custom SMTP setting, outgoing email is sent to the SMTP server entered by that administrator when an email is sent. Depending on the email being sent, this can include recipient email addresses, sender details, subject lines, message content, and technical email headers.

The SMTP server is not supplied by FlowMail Campaigns and is not required for the plugin to work. Site administrators who enter their own SMTP server details should review the terms and privacy policy for that chosen mail provider.

The plugin also includes an admin-only WP-Cron loopback diagnostic. When an administrator runs that diagnostic, the site sends a request to its own wp-cron.php URL to confirm that scheduled tasks can run. No FlowPress service is contacted for this check.

The Reviews screen includes a manual Google-style review badge and a copy/paste importer for reviews that an administrator chooses to copy from their public Google review page. This feature does not contact Google, does not scrape Google, and does not use a Google API key.
